items.title: Async functions and await need typed Rust lowering or an explicit async blocker
Native Node runtime adapters and CommonJS boundaries block JavaScript-to-Rust ports
Make CI on main green and enforced, validate before push, and generate Rust from JavaScript instead of writing it twice
items.body:
## Problem

meta-language is the translator that other Rust projects are meant to use to get Rust from JavaScript (link-assistant/router#759). It applies that standard to itself only in part. The JavaScript/Rust parity gate and the `js` -> `rust` job order in `ci.yml` exist and work. But the Rust code is still mostly written by hand next to the JavaScript, the `CI` workflow has no green run on any branch including `main`, nothing requires it to pass before a merge, and pushes are not checked locally, so each CI failure is found one push at a time.

## Findings

1. **Rust is written twice by hand; only one module is generated.** `rust/src` has 122,747 lines of Rust and `js/src` has 48,042 lines of JavaScript. The only Rust generated from JavaScript with a regenerate-and-diff check is `rust/src/translation/frontend_rules.rs` (534 lines; `npm run check:frontend-rules`, see `docs/self-translation.md`). The per-module `Self-Translation Report` (8 shards in `ci.yml`) only measures how far the translation is from the hand-written Rust. It does not fail when the two differ and does not make the Rust come from the translation.
2. **`CI` has no green run on any branch, including `main`.** Of the last 100 `CI` runs, 0 succeeded (`gh run list --workflow CI`): `main` 3/3 failed (2026-10-06, 2026-10-08 x2), `issue-195-*` 0/28, `issue-199-58f3573d6122` (PR #201, draft, +134,131/-5,667, 58 commits, open since 2026-10-07) 0/44 (25 failed, 19 cancelled), `issue-199-679a3b3c3c56` 0/11, `issue-202-203-*` 0/9, `issue-217-*` 0/5. PR #216 was merged into `main` while `CI` was red (head `eb0574d`, run 37799195371: `Post-merge Report` and `Full Requirements Aggregate` failed, `issue-195: 310/323 requirements passed`).
3. **Nothing requires green CI to merge.** `GET /repos/link-foundation/meta-language/branches/main/protection` returns 404. The only ruleset, `safety`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`; it has no required status checks and no pull request rule. `Full Requirements Aggregate` is described in `ci.yml` as "a required check", but it is not required by any rule.
4. **The failures are different on each run and are found only in CI.** Run 37998880234 (PR #201, 2026-10-09 22:24): `JavaScript Tests (grammar)` failed on `the native Go fixture is current` (`parity/fixtures/native-grammars/go.json is stale; run node scripts/generate-native-grammar-fixtures.mjs`), and `JavaScript Package` failed on the same stale-fixture check (`npm run check:native-grammars`). Run 37984660603: `not ok 262 - native Python matches the independent oracle on every pinned upstream corpus input`. Run 37939535878: that Python test plus `not ok 50 - formal-ai regression: every JavaScript documents entry digests to the Rust golden`. A stale generated file is a one-command local check, yet it failed the whole run. The hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` only cleans caches; there is no `pre-push` hook or documented command that runs `npm run check` and the grammar test group before a push.
5. **No single push gate, and every new push cancels the running stage.** `ci.yml` uses `cancel-in-progress: true` for pull requests at the workflow level and in every job (lines 27-29, 193-195, ...); `js.yml` and `rust.yml` do the same for the Rust stage. 19 of the 44 runs on PR #201 were cancelled before finishing. `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` do not describe a rule that drafts are bulk and only one agent pushes after collecting all failures of the last run (they only set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`).
6. **No workflow-gate check.** `ci.yml` makes `rust` depend on `js` (`needs: [changes, js]`), but nothing fails if a later edit lets a Rust job start without the JavaScript stage. Also, the `changes` job skips the Rust workflow for JavaScript-only changes through a path filter (`ci.yml` lines 40-57); this is acceptable only because the JavaScript stage has the parity check, and that dependency is not tested.
7. **Template workflows are missing.** Compared with link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template, `.github/workflows` has no `links.yml` (link check), `security.yml`, or `workflows.yml` (workflow lint), and the repository has no `.github/zizmor.yml`, `.github/codeql/`, `.lycheeignore` or `.github/dependabot.yml`. Only `secretlint` runs (`js.yml:275`, `rust.yml:164`). No workflow runs `actionlint`, `zizmor`, CodeQL, `cargo audit` or `cargo deny`.
8. **No measurement.** There is no before/after report of pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, or local peak RSS/disk (router#759 requirement 7).

## Requirements

1. Make `CI` on `main` green and keep it green: fix the causes in findings 2 and 4 (stale `parity/fixtures/native-grammars/go.json`, the native Python oracle test, the formal-ai documents digest, the `issue-195` acceptance count). Done when the last 3 `CI` runs on `main` are `success`.
2. Add a ruleset or branch protection for `main` that requires `Full Requirements Aggregate` (and the pull request rule). A pull request with a failed or cancelled `CI` run must not be mergeable. Done when `gh api repos/link-foundation/meta-language/rulesets` lists a `required_status_checks` rule.
3. Generate Rust from JavaScript. Publish in `parity/` a list of modules that are generated (starting with `frontend_rules.rs`) and extend it module by module; each generated module has a `--check` regenerate-and-diff command in `npm run check` and is marked as generated in the Rust file. Make the `Self-Translation Report` fail when a module listed as generated differs from its translation. Hand-written Rust that has no generated counterpart is listed in the parity manifest with the translator issue that blocks it (#204-#213, #219, #220 and others).
4. Add a local pre-push check (a `.githooks/pre-push` installed by `scripts/install-dev-hooks.mjs`, plus one documented command) that runs every `--check` script in `npm run check` and the test groups that touched files affect. Done when the stale `go.json` case fails locally.
5. Document the push gate in `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`: drafting agents never push; one agent pushes once after collecting all failures of the last finished run; no push while a run on the same branch is in progress; JavaScript checks run locally and Rust builds locally only for Rust-only changes. Use a shared bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
6. Stop cancelling a Rust stage that has started: for pull requests, `cancel-in-progress` is true only for the JavaScript stage or a queued Rust stage not yet started; a Rust run that passed its gate finishes. Done when a push during a Rust run does not leave a `cancelled` Rust job.
7. Add a CI check (script in `js/scripts`, run in the JavaScript stage) that parses `.github/workflows/*.yml` and fails if any Rust job can start without `needs:` on the JavaScript jobs, or if a path filter can skip the parity and translation checks.
8. Add the missing template workflows and files (`links.yml`, `security.yml` with `zizmor`/CodeQL/dependency audit, `workflows.yml` with `actionlint`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `.lycheeignore`, `.github/dependabot.yml` for GitHub Actions) or document in `docs/ci-cd/` why a file is not needed.
9. Add `docs/case-studies/` data for PR #201 and `main`: pushes, runs (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first green run, and the same numbers after requirements 1-7.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (standard for big Rust projects; this repository is the translator and the first adopter)
- #199 (remaining #195 scope including self-translation) and PR #201 (the red branch)
- #204, #205, #206, #207, #208, #209, #210, #211, #212, #213, #214, #215, #217, #219, #220 (translator gaps that keep Rust hand-written; requirement 3 depends on them, but none covers the gate, the lists, or the checks)
- #197 (dependency freshness in CI, partly covers finding 7)
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template (workflow files in finding 7)

---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

items.title: Self-translation: an import names items its module does not translate (use crate::m::{a, b} with b unbound)
items.body:
## Problem

At eb0574d5, `import { a, b } from './m.mjs'` becomes `use crate::m::{a, b};` even when `options.imports` gives no signature for `b`, either because `m` carries `b` or because no signatures were passed. The `use` then names an item the translated Rust does not have, so the module does not compile. Upstream already carries every item that uses `b`, so nothing needs `b` in Rust.

In formal-ai (133 modules, imports bound from each module's `selfTranslationSignatures`), most translated import declarations name at least one unbound item. Without signatures, 264 of 289 do.

## Expected

The `use` lists only the bound names. An import that has none left is carried with a diagnostic, such as `import of names m does not translate`.

## Workaround in formal-ai

`scripts/lib/translation-workarounds.mjs` (`import-pruning`) drops the unbound names. When none is left, it carries the import. The ledger counts these items apart from upstream's.

items.title: Self-translation: a module's own helper paths are crate-rooted (crate::ml_*) while its imports name sibling modules (use crate::m::…), so no crate holds both
selfTranslate writes a long Rust expression on one line; wrap it (vec! literals reach 1,250 characters)
items.body:
### Problem

`selfTranslate(source, 'JavaScript', 'Rust')` (main at `679a3b3c`) emits each translated item's Rust on as few lines as the emitter's statement structure gives, so a long expression stays on one line however long it is. An array or object literal is the usual case: the JavaScript source spreads it over several lines, and the Rust comes out as a single line.

From link-assistant/formal-ai's committed projection of `js/agentic/crate/es_tokenizer.mjs`:

```js
const PUNCTUATORS = [
  '>>>=', '...', '===', '!==', '**=', '<<=', '>>=', '>>>', '&&=', '||=', '??=', '=>', '==', '!=',
  '<=', '>=', '&&', '||', '??', '?.', '++', '--', '+=', '-=', '*=', '/=', '%=', '&=', '|=', '^=',
  '<<', '>>', '**', '{', '}', '(', ')', '[', ']', ';', ',', '<', '>', '+', '-', '*', '/', '%',
  '&', '|', '^', '!', '~', '?', ':', '=', '.', '@', '#',
];
```

becomes one Rust line of about 1,250 characters:

```rust
pub static PUNCTUATORS: std::sync::LazyLock<Vec<String>> = std::sync::LazyLock::new(|| vec![String::from(">>>="), String::from("..."), /* … 58 more … */ String::from("#")]);
```

In formal-ai's 128 translated modules, 11 projections hold such a line, the longest at 1,250 characters (nested `vec![vec![vec![…]]]` in `protocol_responses.rs`, 1,159). `rustfmt` would reflow them, but a consumer cannot run it over the output without breaking the byte-exact match against `selfTranslate`, and each translated block is keyed by the SHA-256 of its emitted lines.

### Consumer need

link-assistant/formal-ai requires every committed code file to be human-readable multi-line code ([link-assistant/formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188), requirement R1188-U23, gate `scripts/check-readable-code.mjs`: no line over 300 characters of code). Its translation projections (`rust/tests/fixtures/js-rust-translation/**`) are byte-for-byte upstream output, so until the emitter wraps, they are listed as an exemption that names this issue.

### Request

1. Wrap long Rust output deterministically, the way `rustfmt` would at its default 100-column width: one element per line for a `vec![…]` (or struct literal, or call argument list) that does not fit, nested lists indented by four spaces.
2. Or keep the JavaScript source's own line breaks for literals that span lines in the source.
3. Either way the output stays deterministic, so a consumer can hold its committed Rust byte-equal to the translator.

Acceptance: no line of `selfTranslate` Rust output is longer than 100 characters unless a single token (a string literal) is longer, and the formal-ai projections then pass its readability gate without the exemption.

---
Found while delivering R1188-U23 in [link-assistant/formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188).

items.title: selfTranslate parses each module twice at about 5 KB/s; parse once and speed up the lossless JavaScript parse
items.body:
### Problem

`selfTranslate` (main at `679a3b3c`, `js/src/self-translation.js`) parses the whole source twice with the lossless parser. `LinkNetwork.parse(text, from).reconstructText()` only checks that the links reproduce the source. Then `topLevelItems` calls `parseProgrammingLanguage(text, language)` again to cut the items. Each parse runs at about 5 KB/s, linear in the size of the source. The portable-core work per item (`parseJavaScript`, `checkProgram`, the emitters) takes milliseconds.

Measured on a module of N identical JSDoc-typed functions (node 20, one thread, on a busy 12-core laptop):

| items | bytes | `LinkNetwork.parse` | `parseProgrammingLanguage` | `selfTranslate` total |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 25 | 3,405 | 660 ms | 566 ms | 1,202 ms |
| 50 | 6,830 | 1,255 ms | 1,213 ms | 2,618 ms |
| 100 | 13,680 | 2,606 ms | 2,606 ms | 5,160 ms |
| 200 | 27,580 | 5,037 ms | 5,398 ms | 10,432 ms |

A real 33 KB module (`algorithm_discovery.mjs` in link-assistant/formal-ai) takes 11.5 s in `LinkNetwork.parse` and 9.8 s in `parseProgrammingLanguage`. `docs/self-translation.md` says the report over meta-language's own `js/src` "takes over an hour on one runner" and needs eight CI shards. Almost all of that time is these two parses.

### Consumer need

link-assistant/formal-ai re-translates its 123 JavaScript modules (814 KB) on every change, to hold the committed Rust to the translator ([link-assistant/formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188), the `js-rust` job of `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml`). That takes about 7.5 CPU-minutes, so the job needs four worker threads to stay within its budget. A developer re-translating one edited module waits 10-35 s for it. At tokenizer speed the job would take seconds and could run inside the ordinary JavaScript test tier.

### Request

1. Parse once: build the link network from the same tree `topLevelItems` uses (or cut the items from the network), so the reproduction check costs no second parse.
2. Profile the lossless JavaScript parse. 5 KB/s is about three orders of magnitude slower than a JavaScript tokenizer. Issue #193 was the same kind of hot spot on the Rust side (`point_at_byte` rescanning the source for every span).
3. Optionally, let `selfTranslate` take a pre-parsed network, so a consumer that already parsed the module can reuse it.

Acceptance: `selfTranslate` on the 200-item module above is at least ten times faster, and the output is byte-identical.

---
Found while wiring the js -> rust leg in [link-assistant/formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188) (`docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/js-rust-translation.md`).

items.title: Self-translation items should keep the portable-core diagnostic, not only its kind
items.body:
### Problem

When the portable core refuses an item, `translateGroup` (`js/src/self-translation.js`, main at `679a3b3c`) records only the error's kind. The item list says `carried` with reason `unsupported`, `type` or `syntax`, and the output marker says `// meta-language:carried JavaScript export_statement (unsupported)`. The `TranslationError` it caught already names the construct, the reason and the span (`arrow function: functions as values are outside the portable core at 82..95`), and that is dropped.

### Consumer need

link-assistant/formal-ai ratchets its js -> rust translation and keeps a census of what keeps items out, so it can widen its JavaScript toward the portable core where that pays most ([link-assistant/formal-ai#1188](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1188), `data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino`). To get the construct, it runs `translateProgram` a second time on every carried item's source lines and reads `diagnostic.message`: 1,926 extra translations per run. Two runs of the same item can only be assumed, not shown, to fail for the same reason. The upstream per-module report (`generate-self-translation-report.mjs`) has the same limit: it counts items by status, not by construct.

### Request

1. Keep the diagnostic in the item record: `{ status: 'carried', reason: 'unsupported', construct: 'arrow function', message: '…', span: { start, end } }`, with the span relative to the source.
2. Put the construct in the carried marker, e.g. `// meta-language:carried JavaScript export_statement (unsupported: arrow function)`. A round trip still restores the item, because the marker is not part of the hashed code.
3. Count carried items by construct in the self-translation report, so the most frequent missing constructs come out of the report, not out of each consumer's reconstruction.

---

JavaScript lexer misreads regex literals as malformed numbers or unterminated strings; regex subset support (84 carried items in formal-ai)

Portable core: arrow functions and closures as values inside function bodies (99 carried items in formal-ai)
items.body:
## Construct

Functions as values: arrow functions and function expressions passed as arguments or bound to locals. They are refused with `arrow function: functions as values are outside the portable core`. Without them, the array methods (`.map`, `.filter`, `.some`, `.find`; see the array-method issue), sort comparators and local helpers cannot translate either.

## Count in formal-ai

- `arrow function`: **96**
- `call of a computed function`: **2**
- `method in an object value`: **1**

The wider measurement counts 136. Note that a *top-level* `const f = (x) => …` already translates as a function. Only arrows inside bodies are refused.

## Minimal input

```js
/**
 * @param {number[]} values
 * @param {number} factor
 * @returns {number[]}
 */
export function scaled(values, factor) {
  const scale = (value) => value * factor;
  return [scale(values[0]), scale(values[1])];
}
```

## Expected Rust

```rust
pub fn scaled(values: Vec<f64>, factor: f64) -> Vec<f64> {
    let scale = |value: f64| value * factor;
    vec![
        scale(crate::ml_array::at(&values, crate::ml_array::number_index(0f64))),
        scale(crate::ml_array::at(&values, crate::ml_array::number_index(1f64))),
    ]
}
```

## Suggested direction

- Closures that capture immutable locals map to Rust closures (`impl Fn`). Lean and Rocq take them as `fun`.
- Closures that are only called, or only passed to a known higher-order builtin, need no boxing.
- A closure that escapes (is returned or stored) can be `Box<dyn Fn>` or stay refused with its own diagnostic.

---

**Where this comes from.** [formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai) translates its JavaScript modules to Rust with `selfTranslate(source, 'JavaScript', 'Rust')` from meta-language `main` at `679a3b3c` (PR #196), through [`scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/a75bf377287664599d506921a30bd3bc37410022/scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs). In scope are 128 modules (`js/agentic/crate/*.mjs` and the meta reasoner): 249 of 2,369 top-level items translate and 2,120 are carried. The census counts the construct `translateProgram` names first for each carried item: [`data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/a75bf377287664599d506921a30bd3bc37410022/data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino). The per-item projections are in [`rust/tests/fixtures/js-rust-translation/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/a75bf377287664599d506921a30bd3bc37410022/rust/tests/fixtures/js-rust-translation). A wider measurement adds the agentic planner, the server and the browser worker, 232 more modules: 819 of 6,556 items translate there.

The repro above was checked with `selfTranslate` at `679a3b3c`. The umbrella for this work is #199, section 1. This issue is the one construct, with a minimal case to test against.

Finish the remaining issue #195 scope after PR #196: self-translation, native grammars for every language, multi-source merging, interchange, semantics and release
items.body:
## Goal

PR #196 delivers a large part of issue #195: native grammars for 21 languages, executor recovery, shared concepts, decorators, grammar import, export and merge, CI order, and the post-merge release path. It was merged before the work was finished, with the Full Requirements Aggregate still red. This issue lists **everything that still has to be fully delivered**. Each item must be implemented with real behavior, verified by tests in both runtime packages, and recorded in the requirement ledger (`parity/issue-195-requirements.json`). PR #196 was merged as `679a3b3c` on 2026-10-06, and its `Fixes #195` closed #195, although #195 asked to stay open until delivery evidence exists. **This issue carries the whole remaining scope of #195** until every item below is done. It was checked against the #195 body and all 23 maintainer comments on PR #196: about 270 extracted requirements, each mapped to ledger rows and their last evaluated status.

**Fix first:** at merge, the last CI run on `ddcde321` ([run 37530607538](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37530607538)) failed the JavaScript test `the scope gate reads the full committed ledger after it grows beyond the default subprocess buffer`, so the acceptance stages never ran on the merged head. Make `main` green, then re-run the full evaluation. At PR #196's last fully evaluated run ([run 37503230222](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37503230222)), every build, test and evidence stage passed. **Full Requirements Aggregate: 306/321**, with 0 gate errors. The 15 open pre-merge rows are listed below. The 5 post-merge rows (section 5) were never evaluated. Their implementation entry points are still `null` in `js/scripts/issue-195-vision-requirements.mjs`, because the code does not exist yet.

The detailed requirements come from PR #196's maintainer comments, which remain authoritative. The main ones:

- [5965533606](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965533606): CI and release design, native grammars, shared concepts
- [5971613170](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5971613170): JavaScript first, self-translation, decorators, CI order
- [5979473773](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5979473773)
- [5985077141](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5985077141): memory budget and recovery
- [6023909737](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-6023909737): no intentional red; remaining work

---

## 1. Self-translation: JavaScript/TypeScript ↔ Rust through meta-language

**Rows:** `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-TOOL`, `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-CARRIED-ZERO`, `I195-SELF-TRANSLATION-SHARED-CORPUS`

**State:**

- Across 119 modules, **26 items are translated and 3,347 carried** (about 0.8 %).
- 16 Rust functions are written, **0 identical** to the hand-written Rust, and 61 of 210 translated lines are shared.
- The last sessions added only small features: string methods, case mapping, trims, `\u` escapes, default parameters and top-level constants.

**To do:**

- [ ] Implement the most frequent carried constructs **in one batch, generically, in JavaScript first**:
  - `export class` and classes, objects and `new`;
  - closures and higher-order functions;
  - destructuring and spread;
  - `Map`/`Set`, iterators and generators;
  - template literals;
  - `try`/`catch`/`throw`;
  - modules, imports and exports;
  - async functions.
- [ ] Bring **carried to 0** for every `js/src` module, with a per-module report published on every CI run.
- [ ] Replace hand-written Rust modules with generated ones, module by module, once they pass `cargo check`, clippy and the shared Links Notation parity corpus. From then on, Rust changes come from translation, not hand-written mirrors.
- [ ] Use decorators to make generated Rust match the project's style. Drive "identical functions" and "shared lines" toward 100 %.
- [ ] Round-trip tests exercise **translated** items, separately from blocks restored from source text by hash:
  - same-language round trips are byte-identical;
  - cross-language round trips preserve behavior.
- [ ] Translate full JavaScript/TypeScript ↔ Rust programs, not only fixtures. Export the capability as a library API and a CLI in both packages.

## 2. Native grammars for every catalog language

**Rows:** `I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-MERGED`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES`, `I195-GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`, `I195-DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED`

**State:**

- **Native by default (21):** C, CSV, Diff, Go, GraphQL, INI, Java, JavaScript, JSON, JSON5, Lean, Make, Protocol Buffers, Racket, Regex, Rocq, Rust, Scheme, Solidity, TSX, TypeScript.
- **Bulk matrix:** 67/67 tree-sitter grammars import, 38 accept their sample and 24 match the oracle.
- **29 reject their sample:** Markdown, DOCX, Python, C#, R, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Perl, Haskell, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Dart, Agda, CMake, Elixir, Elm, HCL, MATLAB, Nix, Odin, PowerShell, HTML, CSS, YAML, TOML, XML, DTD.

**To do:**

- [ ] **Automatic external-scanner porting.** Most rejections come from missing `scanner.c` behavior; Python, for example, reports `_newline`, `_indent`, `_dedent` and `string_start` as unsupported. Do one of the following, then regenerate all affected languages in one batch:
  - read each pinned `scanner.c` through the native C grammar and translate it into native scanner rules; or
  - implement the common scanner families once, generically: indentation and layout, heredocs, string interpolation, nested comments, raw strings.
- [ ] Every catalog language with a grammar source parses **natively by default** in both runtimes and matches its oracle. It produces a lossless CST (kinds, fields, tokens, trivia, spans, error and missing nodes, embedded languages) and an optional AST with provenance. The trees reload without the source, can be edited, and emit and re-parse.
- [ ] **Remove production tree-sitter.** `web-tree-sitter` is still in `js/package.json` `dependencies`, and `rust/Cargo.toml` still has 36 `tree-sitter*` crates in `[dependencies]`. Keep them only as dev/test oracles. The final production count is **0**, and no vendored grammar binaries are shipped.
- [ ] Changing a native grammar rule changes the public parse result with no host-code patch, and no external engine, subprocess or download runs at parse time.
- [ ] **Built-in formats and grammar-description languages are catalog entries too** ([5895896874](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5895896874)):
  - built-in formats: LiNo, txt, Markdown, PDF and DOCX;
  - grammar-description languages: BNF, EBNF, ABNF, PEG, Peggy, Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications.

  Each needs a native Links Notation grammar and tests. **A host-coded parser does not count as native merely because it is called that.**
- [ ] **Natural languages (10 entries).** Define in `docs/vision.md` and the row text what their native representation is, with tests. Every ledger row must have a satisfiable, tested definition; clarify ambiguous rows while keeping their full intent, and never leave a row impossible to pass.
- [ ] Catalog: versions, editions, dialects, aliases, extensions and embedded languages, with every grammar source pinned with license, provenance and independent corpora.

## 3. Real multi-source merging

**Rows:** `I195-MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE`, `I195-MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`

**State:** reconciliation works: 1,486 shared rules across the 39 languages with two or more sources. But **28 languages have a single source**: Markdown, Lean, Rocq, Python, TSX, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Ruby, Perl, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Bash, Agda, Diff, Elm, Groovy, Make, Nix, PowerShell, Racket, Scheme, four SQL dialects, YAML, DTD and INI.

**To do:**

- [ ] Inventory and import every mature source per language: official specification grammars, grammars-v4, tree-sitter, and the languages' own parsers (Lean, Rocq, the Python PEG grammar and others).
- [ ] A non-interactive pipeline discovers, merges and reconciles the sources into shared concepts, with a reproducible decision report.
- [ ] Shipped grammars are **outputs of the pipeline**, not single-source imports with hand edits.
- [ ] A test fails when a merge only concatenates its sources.

## 4. Other open rows

- [ ] **`I195-ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES`:** each native grammar runs against several independent oracles (tree-sitter, ANTLR, official compilers and provers) on pinned corpora and real projects. Every discrepancy is traced to a test.
- [ ] **`I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES`:** every feature of BNF, EBNF, ABNF, PEG, Peggy, Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications has a native representation and operational meaning. Imports follow included grammars, lexers, scanners and actions.
- [ ] **`I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS`:** cross-format and native → external → native cycles run under the actual target tools, installed in CI. Accepted and rejected inputs, structure, precedence, actions and diagnostics are compared.
- [ ] **`I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY`:** the full JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq construct inventory (classes, mutation, standard library, imports, async, ownership, macros and notation, types, universes, effects, proofs and tactics) is represented and transformed through the common links. Normal JavaScript is accepted without annotations.
- [ ] **Translation for the full languages, not the portable core.** On `main`, `js/src/translation/emit-common.js` still translates a "checked portable-core program". `ASSUMPTIONS.inBoundsReads` limits agreement to executions whose array reads are in bounds, and the targets abort where JavaScript reads `undefined`. Encode the out-of-bounds behavior faithfully and remove the assumption. Extend all 12 directed translations (JavaScript, Rust, Lean, Rocq), in both packages, to the full languages with project-wide binding, type, universe and effect analysis, macro and notation expansion with hygiene, and proof and tactic elaboration. The passing `I195-SEM-*` and `I195-TRANSLATE-*` rows cover today's fixtures; they must also hold on real projects.
- [ ] **`I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS`:** formal-ai's TypeScript ↔ Rust/JavaScript projection pairs translate through shared concepts on clean installed artifacts. A TypeScript CST alone does not count.

## 5. Release

These post-merge rows were never evaluated: `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED` and `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK`.

- [ ] **Publish.** CI on `main` publishes the crate and the npm package from the release tag. npm still serves only `0.46.0`, and the earlier `main` publish failed with `ENEEDAUTH` under OIDC. Document the exact npm trusted-publisher settings the workflow needs, and resolve the continuing publication problem of #171.
- [ ] **Verify the published packages.** Install from npm and crates.io, run the four-language examples from the published packages, and verify checksums and offline-first public APIs. Run RML (PR #184 workloads) and formal-ai against the **published** versions, so that downstream users get the release out of the box.
- [ ] **Merge rule.** Ruleset 24204187, which required Full Requirements Aggregate on `main`, was removed so that PR #196 could merge. Once the pre-merge rows pass, re-create a rule that requires the PR checks on the default branch. Its post-merge report on `main` verifies it with data the workflow token can read.
- [ ] **Dependency freshness.** The scheduled job on `main` keeps every retained dependency current (see #197). Resolve the Rocq/OCaml toolchain and build-image constraints with a reproducible solution: "held by another dependency" describes work to do, not a reason to stay behind.
- [ ] **Memory regression checks.** Each memory fix (the parse memo budget, lazy grammar loading, reuse of the inline Markdown parser, compact offset maps, streamed parity evidence) has a bounded-heap or peak-RSS regression check in CI. Where formal-ai's workloads blew past their memory limit, record the cause and keep its regression test.

---

## Rules for whoever works on this (people and AI agents)

1. **Every session delivers real implementation progress** on the items above. A red check means unfinished work to implement now. It is never intended, never a reason to stop, and never a reason to weaken, skip or re-classify a requirement.
2. **Work in bulk, not one small feature per session.** Pick a whole item, such as the next batch of carried constructs or automatic scanner porting, and finish it.
3. **JavaScript first.** Develop and debug in JavaScript; port to Rust in one batch, by self-translation wherever possible. Never mirror commit by commit.
4. **Automate:** importers, merging, scanner porting, the translator and generators, instead of hand-writing grammars or Rust. Make each fix generic, then regenerate everything it affects.
5. **Bulk pushes.** Draft the whole batch, commit locally, re-read the diff, then push once. While CI runs, continue with the next item, and fix every reported failure in one batch.
6. **CI** stays as designed:
   - JavaScript runs first, and Rust and acceptance only after it passes;
   - every failure is reported in one run;
   - only pre-merge checks run on pull requests;
   - `main` produces the release.
7. **Resources.** Earlier sessions were killed for running out of memory.
   - Locally, run only targeted JavaScript tests, plus one `cargo check` when porting, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, wrapped in `node scripts/with-cache-cleanup.mjs`.
   - Never run locally: the full suites, acceptance, coverage, the bulk pipeline, self-translation reports, the formal-ai or RML workloads, or whole-corpus experiments.
   - Run `node scripts/clean-caches.mjs` after each batch, kill leftover `cargo`, `rustc`, `node`, `lean` and `rocq` processes, and commit early.
8. Split this issue into smaller pull requests per item if that helps. Every pull request must be green before merge.

Related: #195, #196. Also #197 (dependency updates and freshness) and #198 (no_std ECMAScript tokenizer and lossless JS/TS ↔ link-network pivot), which overlap with sections 1, 2 and 5.

items.title: Provide a no_std ECMAScript tokenizer and a lossless JS/TS <-> link-network pivot for WASM consumers
items.body:
## Summary

Consumers that must parse and render JavaScript/TypeScript in WASM (where tree-sitter grammars do not build) write their own lexer and pivot. link-assistant/formal-ai keeps `rust/src/es_tokenizer.rs` (736 lines: `no_std` ECMAScript tokenizer with regex/division disambiguation and template parts) and `rust/src/es_meta.rs` (863 lines: JS/TS ↔ Links Notation pivot driven by projection rules). This is the same representation job this crate exists for.

## What to do

Provide a `no_std` + `alloc` ECMAScript tokenizer and token-tree ↔ link-network pivot in this crate (a feature or a sibling crate in this repository), lossless for JS and TS source, so every consumer uses one implementation. Related: #195 (full four-language representation; CST by default for all languages).

## How to test

Round trip source → network → source is byte-identical for a corpus of JS/TS files, built for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.


---
Found by a duplication audit of link-assistant/formal-ai against the dependencies its maintainers own (consumer-side tracking: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1182; the audit table there lists the code this issue lets Formal AI delete). Per the organizations' policy, general logic belongs in the dependency so every consumer gets it out of the box and consumer code shrinks.

items.title: Update all dependencies to their latest releases (links-notation 0.13->0.22, tree-sitter 0.25->0.27, lindera 3->6, 6 more) and enforce freshness in CI
items.body:
## Summary

Every dependency of this repository should be at its latest release (the maintainers' standing requirement, applied first in link-assistant/formal-ai#1169, which also tracks this update as a consumer). `meta-language` 0.58.2 (latest release) and `rust/Cargo.toml` on `main` (checked 2026-09-29) declare nine dependencies whose latest release is outside the declared range:

| Dependency | Declared | Latest release |
|---|---|---|
| `links-notation` | 0.13 | 0.22.0 |
| `tree-sitter` | 0.25.8 | 0.27.0 |
| `tree-sitter-graphql` | 0.1.0 | 0.2.1 |
| `tree-sitter-lua` | 0.2.0 | 0.5.0 |
| `tree-sitter-proto` | 0.4.0 | 0.6.0 |
| `tree-sitter-scala` | 0.25.1 | 0.26.2 |
| `ts-parser-perl` | 1.1.2 | 2.0.0 |
| `doublets` | 0.4.0 | 0.5.0 |
| `lindera` | 3.0.7 | 6.2.0 |

Because of the `links-notation` pin, every consumer that also uses current `links-notation` compiles two copies (0.13.0 and the current one), and Links Notation values cannot flow between `meta-language` networks and the consumer's own `links-notation` types without conversion.

## Requirements

1. R1: update all nine to their latest releases and adapt the code; the tree-sitter 0.27 bump must keep every grammar crate on a compatible `tree-sitter-language` ABI (upgrade the other grammar crates in the same change, and list any grammar that has no 0.27-compatible release as a blocker with its upstream issue).
2. R2: `cargo update` leaves no semver-compatible update pending (`cargo update --dry-run` prints no `Updating` lines).
3. R3: CI job that fails when a direct dependency is behind without an open issue URL on the pin line (`cargo install cargo-outdated --locked && cargo outdated --root-deps-only --exit-code 1`; `npm outdated` for the JavaScript package).
4. R4: publish the release to crates.io and npm.

## How to test

`cargo tree -i links-notation` in a crate depending on the new `meta-language` release and on `links-notation` 0.22 shows a single version; the existing CST round-trip tests pass for every grammar.
